claims.note: The source confirms an agent translates GPU kernels to Rust at 99.5% of original performance; 'NVIDIA' is not named verbatim but the context (cuTile, TileGym, CUDA) is NVIDIA's ecosystem and the attribution is a reasonable paraphrase.

claims.claim: NVIDIA's cuTile-rs uses a multi-agent pipeline to translate GPU kernels from Python or Triton into Rust
claims.summary_span: NVIDIA's cuTile-rs uses a multi-agent pipeline to translate GPU kernels from Python or Triton into Rust
claims.source_span: our team built an AI agent skill that translates cuTile Python and Triton-TileIR kernels into cuTile Rust. Each conversion starts from whichever reference implementation the operator has (cuTile Python or Triton-TileIR) and runs through a bounded multi-agent pipeline covering analysis, the device kernel, host and FFI code, and benchmarking.
claims.note: Source confirms multi-agent pipeline translating cuTile Python and Triton-TileIR to cuTile Rust; 'cuTile-rs' matches 'cutile-rs' in source.

claims.claim: gaining memory-safety guarantees without touching the underlying compiler
claims.summary_span: gaining memory-safety guarantees without touching the underlying compiler
claims.source_span: Extending the Rust ownership model to tile-based GPU kernels... porting a kernel to cuTile Rust is not a re-optimization problem. It is re-expressing the same tile program in a safer host language, with the same compiler and the same performance model underneath.
claims.note: Source confirms safety comes from Rust's ownership model while the same underlying compiler (tileiras) is used unchanged.

claims.claim: All 24 TileGym operators are ported at 99.5% of original performance
claims.summary_span: All 24 TileGym operators are ported at 99.5% of original performance
claims.source_span: we ported all 24 public TileGym operators to cuTile Rust and reached 99.5% of cuTile Python performance on average.
claims.note: Source directly states all 24 operators ported at 99.5% of cuTile Python performance on average.

claims.claim: The translation skill ships in the TileGym repo
claims.summary_span: The translation skill ships in the TileGym repo
claims.source_span: The skill ships in the TileGym repo, so you can apply it to your own kernels.
claims.note: Source directly confirms the skill ships in the TileGym repo.

claims.claim: GPU kernel authoring in Rust required manual translation; an agent now handles all 24 production operators.
claims.summary_span: GPU kernel authoring in Rust required manual translation; an agent now handles all 24 production operators.
claims.source_span: our team built an AI agent skill that translates cuTile Python and Triton-TileIR kernels into cuTile Rust. Using this skill, we ported all 24 public TileGym operators to cuTile Rust
claims.note: Source confirms an agent now handles translation of all 24 operators; the implication that this was previously manual is consistent with the source describing the agent as a new development to make existing kernels available in Rust.

claims.claim: An agent closes a 40-point gap on real business intelligence questions
claims.summary_span: An agent closes a 40-point gap on real business intelligence questions
claims.source_span: BI-Agent achieves substantial accuracy gains of up to 40 percentage points with vanilla LLMs
claims.note: Source confirms BI-Agent achieves up to 40 percentage point gains on real-world BI questions; 'closes a gap' is a fair paraphrase of accuracy gains.

claims.summary_span: Frontier language models answer fewer than half of real-world business intelligence questions on BI-Bench
